title: Transformer Architecture — Generation Reuses Earlier Work

body:
## Generation Reuses Earlier Work

Generating one token at a time would repeatedly recompute keys and values for the entire prefix. That waste grows with every new token.

A key-value cache stores earlier attention projections so each decoding step computes only the new token’s pieces. The cache grows with layers, sequence length, and key-value heads.

Batching requests improves hardware use, but different prompt and output lengths create scheduling challenges. Serving design is part of transformer performance.
common_mistakes: A transformer contains attention and nothing else.
Decoder generation should read future unseen tokens.
A key-value cache makes memory use shrink as context grows.
mini_exercise: Draw “Generation Reuses Earlier Work” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Transformers are the architecture behind modern language models and many vision and multimodal systems.
explain_back_prompt: Using “Generation Reuses Earlier Work,” explain Transformer Architecture without assuming the listener knows modern AI.
